claims.explanation: GW-441756 is a selective TrkA (NTRK1) inhibitor, so cancer lines that depend on NGF/TrkA autocrine or paracrine signaling for proliferation and survival should be selectively killed. The strongest predictor is high NTRK1 (TrkA) expression, often accompanied by NGF or BDNF ligand expression, as seen in neuroblastoma, Ewing sarcoma, melanoma, and other neural-crest-derived tumors. Conversely, low NTRK1 expression or dependence on other RTK pathways would be protective.

features.basis: GW-441756 is a selective TrkA inhibitor; high TrkA expression predicts dependence on NGF/TrkA signaling (PMID 27145455, 33466524, 31788928)
NGF ligand expression can drive autocrine TrkA activation, making cells sensitive to TrkA inhibition (PMID 27145455, 33466524)
BDNF can activate TrkB but may also contribute to neurotrophin signaling context; Ewing sarcoma expresses BDNF and TrkB (PMID 27145455)
TrkB expression may provide an alternative survival pathway not blocked by selective TrkA inhibition (PMID 27145455)
TrkC expression could compensate for TrkA inhibition via neurotrophin-3 signaling
Ewing sarcoma, driven by EWSR1 fusions, is sensitive to TrkA inhibition (PMID 27145455)
EWSR1-FLI1 fusion defines Ewing sarcoma, which responds to TrkA inhibition (PMID 27145455)
TP53 pathway alterations may reduce dependence on TrkA-mediated survival signals
MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma often has high TrkA expression and neural crest origin
ALK fusions or mutations can provide alternative RTK survival signaling
EGFR-driven lines may not depend on TrkA signaling for survival
SERPINE1 downregulation in virtual cell response suggests its high expression may buffer against drug effect
